summary: Devendra Nath Ojha is an Indologist who completed a certificate in Jyotisha at the National Sanskrit University in 2020. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Delhi (2011–2013) and Head of Sanskrit and assistant professor at Amity University in 2017.
Deviprasad Mishra is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the French Institute of Pondicherry in 1999. In that same year, he served as Deputy Head of Indology and researcher at the institute.
Dewei Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen, attested in 2010.
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima, and later participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dhananjay Vashistha works in Indology and philosophy after earning a B.E. from BITS Pilani (2011–2015). He worked as a network engineer at Cisco Systems (2015–2021), taught at Trans IAS Academy (2021–2023), and became a research associate at Bhaktivedanta Research Center in 2023.

Dharm P. S. Bhawuk works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1992–1995) and became an affiliate faculty member at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1995.

Dharmananda Kosambi (1876–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Harvard University in 1926. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1908), Harvard (~1910–1912), Gujarat University (~1922–1925), and Saint Petersburg State University (~1929–1931).

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1925). He held posts at Patna College in 1928 and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and the traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held teaching posts at Open University (2008–2018), University of Leeds (2015), University of Bristol (2017–2019), and University of Chester (2019).
Di Jiang is a scholar in linguistics, computational fields, and Tibetology. He has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.

Di Luo is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by James Steele for an MA, Di Luo completed a PhD at the University of Southern California (attested 2016) under Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge.

Diana L. Eck is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD ~1976 under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), and had a long career as a professor at Harvard University from ~1976.

Diana Lange is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, Sorbonne, and EPHE. She held positions at TU Berlin, Leipzig, Zurich, Museum am Rothenbaum, Max Planck Institute, Humboldt University, and Hamburg.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. In 2005, she held posts as adjunct professor of anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane Denis is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned a BA from Naropa University (1989–1995) and a PhD from Laval University (2005–2013), and served as associate professor at Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 2017.

Diane E. Riggs is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Myosei Tatsuguchi and completed a PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford (attested 2010). She held posts at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who was a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).
